2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/free-reader#.reason: Part of one correction to the ConfigError arm. The next change set narrows it to the config read, restores exit 3 with its backtrace for a ConfigError raised after a verb has already written the config, updates main's own docstring so the exit contract it states is true of the ConfigError class, and adds the missing case to the exit-contract testset in test/coverage.jl, which today enumerates every arm but the new one.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/under-reject.reason: Accepted in full: placed at the outermost catch the arm cannot tell a bad consumer config from one the tool itself just wrote, and Bump.jl:36 and Init.jl:565 re-read the config immediately after writing it, so exit 3 and its backtrace are lost exactly where they carried information nothing else carries. The next change set catches ConfigError at the config read instead of around the whole verb table, and pins the new branch with a test.

The point stands: the stale prose was the only record that a guard was owed, so deleting it turned an unpaid debt into a settled fact. The next change set restores both as owed. Bank gains the unrostered-lane-file report D10 promised, since a stray findings/NN-lane.json is a scribe writing to the wrong name and this package has been bitten by silent scribe failures before; and the Step-0 text returns to stating that round import needs no config and runs self verify first, marked NOT YET BUILT, so the debt stays visible until cmd_round is taught to skip the config read for that one path.

Two real points. The D11 paragraph now sits at 126 words against the rule's stated 120 and nothing checks it, because prose_shape.jl binds the caps always on a docstring but only on a NEW page unit, leaving a baselined section held by the ratchet alone. The next change set rewrites that paragraph under the cap and reconciles the rule text with what the scan actually enforces. On deliberation, both re-baselines in this round carry their reason in their own commit, which is the discipline asked for.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/behaviour-ch.reason: Same correction as under-rejection#1, and the previously_worked judgement is right: a ConfigError raised mid-verb after side effects returned 3 with a backtrace before this diff and returns 2 with one line after it, for input that was valid. The widening was undeclared in the fix's own comment, which named only the initial-read case.

Accepted as an improvement to the mechanism rather than to this instance. The next change set makes gbg scan docs --rebaseline prose-shape print the rows it is about to raise, so the guarantee a reviewer currently gets only by reading the CSV diff row against the prose diff is produced by the program instead of by hand.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/over-rejecti.reason: Same correction as under-rejection#2. The restriction at Rounds.jl:856 is real and cheap to lift for the one implemented --empty path, so the design promise goes back as owed rather than being rewritten into a description of what the CLI happens to do today.

Accepted: the statement was made current in one direction only. The next change set restores the close refusal to RULE.INST.CARRY, since closing over a finding already carried CARRY_LIMIT times is refused unconditionally at carry_conditions regardless of the pass budget, that is the refusal that bites first, and it is the one the rule's own check in test/rounds.jl actually pins.

The of exemption demonstrably protected nothing: no operator in the eleven scripts or the prelude is followed by a template literal, which the test's own comment records as checked on 2026-09-12. Removing it therefore withdraws cover from no legitimate form while closing the same class the in exemption hid a blocker behind. The guard is test-side, so its failure mode is a loud test failure a session fixes in minutes rather than a shipped defect, and on a frozen-script surface the wider guard is the safer direction. The substring effect the lane notes, that the lookbehinds also exempted words ending in in or of, argues the same way: those were never intended exemptions either.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/public-contr.reason: Correct, and the blocker re-rating is fair: main's docstring is the one home of the exit contract, and it now makes an unconditional claim that is false for the whole ConfigError class. The next change set updates it alongside narrowing the catch, so the contract and the code are corrected together rather than the prose being amended to match a widened behaviour.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/claim-versus.reason: Refused as unfixable in place rather than disputed. c7db4e5 is pushed, and this package does not rewrite or re-issue published history, so the commit's inventory cannot be corrected where it lives. Both unlisted edits, templates/README.md and docs/src/guide/install.md, are individually sound, and this audit's findings.md is now the durable record that the itemisation was incomplete. The lesson binds forward: a fix-pass commit that presents a categorised inventory lists every file it touches.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/contract-dri.reason: A real defect my own removal left behind: D10 now reads or live. An A lane file no roster entry expects, because the deleted text began mid-sentence after the article and the replacement opened a new one. The next change set deletes the orphaned An.

Mine, and simply wrong. I put .gbg/managed.json into the PINNED list whose defining property is that the tool never renders it, while gbg sync rewrites that sidecar on every run. The next change set files managed.json under the MANAGED kind in all three prose homes, the CFG.TORN row in ARCHITECTURE 7.3, preflight step 2, and the pinned_and_managed docstring, or else redefines PINNED as consumer-owned and never rendered from a template and says plainly which side the sidecar falls on. Doctor.pinned_and_managed draws no such line today, so the prose must follow the code rather than invent a taxonomy the code does not have.

Accepted on the strength-of-promise point. The next change set makes the reference match its scope: SCAN.DEAD_REF keeps RULE.DOC.DEAD_REF as its canonical rule, and RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE either drops the scan from its check or qualifies it as covering src docstrings only, with panel retained so the reading-panel debt is not quietly retired. The same qualification applies to RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING and SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE.

Accepted: an edit whose stated purpose was to make the header match the args introduced drift in the one direction that matters. The next change set restores round_dir, which Passes.jl sends in every act args file and deletes on exactly one path, and removes batch, which no CLI path writes. It is an instrument change, so it goes in its own commit and its own release.

The inconsistency is the fair part of this. The next change set picks one house convention and applies it to both: a measured figure in the design record carries the date it was taken, so the ID_RESOLVES counts get theirs and the signature figures return as a dated snapshot instead of a handful.

2026-09-12-audit-changes-01/sweep-comple.reason: A genuine partial sweep of my own class. The next change set links consumer to the install glossary at docs/src/guide/rules.md:7 and docs/src/guide/instruments.md:43, the two guide pages using the identical unglossed term that the first sweep passed over.

Accepted, and the load-bearing half is the one left uncorrected. The next change set brings IMPLEMENTATION.md:290 and the Phase 2 procedure at 644-653 into line with the corrected Step-0 text, since cmd_round reads the config before dispatching every round verb, import --empty included, and a future session follows that plan verbatim.
